title: Realistic entry-fill slip is the cheapest falsifier for a stop-entry edge; run it before any exit/sizing/MC
one_line_lesson: For any stop/break-entry candidate, run a fill-slip sweep (0/0.5/1/1.5 ticks) BEFORE building any exit design, sizing frontier, or first-passage MC -- spread-cost-clearable does not mean fill-robust, and realistic slip is often a larger tax than spread.

title: The honest null for a time-of-day-anchored setup is a same-day time-placebo
one_line_lesson: To test whether a time-anchored intraday setup (opening range, session open) carries anchor-specific edge, the null must hold the day's price scale/volatility/cost fixed and vary only the anchor time -- cross-day rotation breaks on price-scale mismatch; direction-flip tests stop geometry, not the anchor.

title: A deadline-capped challenge is a Sharpe race, not a symmetric first-passage; screen on the edge x frequency ceiling and prefer information-ratio exits
one_line_lesson: A prop-challenge objective (reach +5% before -5% within a horizon) is a Sharpe-race-with-a-deadline, not symmetric first-passage -- screen candidates on the analytic pass-ceiling (edge x frequency vs barrier) before any MC, and prefer highest information-ratio exits over highest-skew exits.
cost_if_repeated: Anchor: a Sharpe-~0.6 ~1-trade/day edge caps at ~58% challenge pass-rate regardless of sizing (computable a-priori, no MC needed). A low-variance give-back-33%-of-open-profit exit (WR 0.755) beat a max-positive-skew lottery exit for the 120-day-capped FXIFY challenge.

title: The DSR selection floor, not the bust/pass gate, is a discovery axis's binding reachability constraint -- governed by K, not sample size
one_line_lesson: Before committing a discovery axis, compute its DSR demonstrability floor at the axis's intrinsic trial count K and benchmark against the best in-house validated edge -- if the floor exceeds it, the axis is dead at the admission gate regardless of how forgiving the downstream survivor geometry is. The floor is governed by K, not n; more data does not help.

title: A parent-process config patch does not cross a process pool
one_line_lesson: Any run whose correctness depends on a mutated module-level constant must apply the mutation INSIDE the worker (after its own re-import), read the value back from the object the engine actually consumes, and assert the attested set is a singleton across every unit of work -- passing a config KEY rather than a resolved value lets a joblib worker silently re-resolve the still-defective on-disk config.

title: Fetch and read origin/main before every multi-step build, before push, and before every irreversible or budget-spending step
one_line_lesson: git fetch origin && git log --oneline origin/main ^HEAD at the start of any multi-step effort (docs included), before authoring any new brief/spec, before push, and immediately before any irreversible step; grep origin/main for an owed item's slug before discharging it; an orphaned or reset-away commit is evidence, not debris.
cost_if_repeated: Six firings 2026-07-11 → 2026-08-05: a PR-2 built on a stale base; a §4 discharge re-asserted 36 minutes after main withdrew it; an operator ask already overtaken by a landed PR; ~2 hours of MNQFLOW-1 execution from a reset-away artifact.

title: Verify 'owed / missing / never-measured' claims against the campaign's own artifacts before reporting them
one_line_lesson: Before reporting any owed or missing claim, grep the campaign directory (RESULTS_stage*.md, calibration JSON, addenda) for the measurement; in multi-agent sweeps give the verifier the explicit axis 'for every owed X, search for X already done'.

title: A quotation from a reader summary is not a quotation; an attributed claim recalled from memory is not a citation
one_line_lesson: Before any quoted string or specific attributed claim (mechanism, scope, count) lands, verify the exact text at the source yourself — rg for repo files, a real fetch for URLs — or drop the quotation marks and attribute the paraphrase; check source dates precede publication; chase repeated statistics to their root.
cost_if_repeated: 2026-08-12: two fabricated registry quotes in a charter, one blessing a forbidden move (BLOCKER). 2026-08-13: the search summarizer fabricated regulatory events and a citation. 2026-08-22: three misattributions from same-session memory in one ADR draft.

title: Absence in a known location is not absence: a negative existence claim needs a class enumeration
one_line_lesson: Before asserting something does not exist, enumerate the class it would live in (ls -d parent/*/, a glob, rg --no-ignore), never a single-path stat; verify a prescribed remedy is possible; say 'found none at X, did not search Y' rather than 'none exists'.
cost_if_repeated: 2026-08-03: a governance tombstone recorded 33 files as unrecoverable with an impossible remedy; a 35/35 hash-verified copy sat in a sibling backup directory one ls away.

title: Ratified text edited alongside an authorized change: partition a governance diff by provenance, not by file
one_line_lesson: When judging a PR that amends a ratified artifact, hash the previously ratified blocks against the ratifying commit and compare; a BLAST-RADIUS: CLEAN table is evidence about intent, not the diff.
cost_if_repeated: 2026-08-15: a pin-mark PR reproduced every mechanical claim and bundled an in-place edit of a Decision (binding) line the operator had GO'd hours earlier.

title: A driver-layer fix leaves the kernel default stale
one_line_lesson: When a verification falsifies more than one pin, check each separately for where the fix landed — kernel default vs driver override; grep the kernel's module literals against the verified values before reusing a 'corrected' harness.
cost_if_repeated: Q-FUNDPOL-1 (found 2026-07-31): the payout minimum was fixed only as a CLI default while gap_stage2_capbound.py kept PAYOUT_MIN = 1_000.0 gating a floor-lock trigger; +2.84pp funded dead-1y alone, +6.29pp with the ladder.

title: Visible restraint: a deliberate 'do not act' goes in the closing brief with its rationale, never as silent absence
one_line_lesson: A closing brief carries actions landed, watch-items deliberately not acted (one-line rationale each), and permanently-off-radar items at equal prominence; later passes start from the inherited watch-items, and a consolidation near a locked file is checked against them first.
cost_if_repeated: 2026-04-29: S6's triplicated STARTING_EQUITY / PROFIT_TARGET was real duplication left in place because it touches Rule-0 files; unrecorded it would resurface as a fresh candidate every pass.

title: An LLM-reviewer fold loop needs a stopping rule; a non-falling finding count is a missing decision, not review noise
one_line_lesson: Count findings per round and stop when the count fails to fall for two rounds or the document grows on a fix round; triage each finding (M-43) and expect pushback; route unchosen operator options out before specifying them; close with one-line folds, an explicit Open-items section, one reply per thread, and merge.
cost_if_repeated: PRs #335/#336 (2026-09-10/11): counts 14,15,11,7,10,14,3,8 and 7,5,5,4,3,4,1,2; pushback 1 partial of 99; the umbrella doubled 66→133 KB, 18→31 packets, 11→16 operator decisions; a Codex 'simplify' re-found five fixed defects in ten minutes.

title: Code-review fold loop on contract-driven code: after two rounds, rebuild from the invariant table
one_line_lesson: For verifier/owner code implementing a written contract, build the invariant table first (claim → named refusal → one test per invariant), check cross-field claims with the whole record in hand, give durable owners one hashed transition function; fold at most two review rounds, then rebuild and take one more round; refuse a feature whose contract evidence does not exist.
cost_if_repeated: PR #395 (2026-09-15): 12,11,5,3,9 findings over five rounds on the settlement owner — every fold locally correct, globally incomplete. PR #401: 5 of 11 round 2–3 findings were created by the round 1–2 folds.

title: A spec with orders, positions or shutdown semantics is folded only once; the second round rebuilds from a state model and event sequences
one_line_lesson: Write first a state table with one writer per state and an explicit UNKNOWN, action classes with the fail-closed rule, end-to-end sequences with a cut at every step, and an event × state matrix; derive requirements from those; check live paths against the qualified emulator semantics; gate on executable sequence tests, not test names.
cost_if_repeated: PR #360 TB-S3 rail spec (2026-09-12): 6→6→7 findings after two paragraph folds; the operator judged a checklist insufficient — the fix is the model. The rebuilt spec's next round still surfaced four conflicting compositions.

title: Stacked PR: request review only after the parent lands, or retarget the child's base
one_line_lesson: After stacking a child on an unmerged parent, do not request review until the parent lands and main is merged back, or retarget the base first; triage parent-content findings to the parent's owner on main; run git diff --stat base...HEAD and confirm every file is this PR's before requesting review.
cost_if_repeated: PR #401 (2026-09-16): four of five round-5 findings were the parent #405's ~70-file diff; when #405 merged an hour later they became defects on main with no PR owning them.

title: Private artifacts inside a worktree die with the worktree
one_line_lesson: A digest is not a copy: every private file a public record pins is registered (docs/evidence/PRIVATE_EVIDENCE.sha256 or a tracked manifest) and archived to first-passage-archive with scripts/evidence_archive.py put, pushed, in the same step. Private outputs still go under the primary checkout's ignored roots, never .worktrees/* or .claude/worktrees/*; before any worktree removal, scripts/repo_hygiene.py lists its ignored entries and removal stops if any remain unarchived. Committing untracked evidence is not preservation (lossy under core.autocrlf=true; a later branch switch deletes the originals) — preserve via evidence_archive.py put; stage any evidence bytes that must be committed with git -c core.autocrlf=false add (the conversion happens at staging, so an override on a commit of already-staged files is too late), and since text/eol attributes still convert, keep such evidence under a -text attribute and confirm the staged blob (git ls-files -s) equals git hash-object --no-filters before committing; verify with evidence_archive.py audit --verify; extract via git cat-file blob, never git archive or checkout.
cost_if_repeated: Fourth firing 2026-09-24: checkpoint commit 272028e blanket-tracked 1,025 untracked recovery/ files; core.autocrlf=true made 252/606 SHA256SUMS pins mismatch as committed and the switch to main deleted the originals (all 606 later restored, verified against their pins and archived; their registration is in PR #492, open at the time of writing). Third firing 2026-09-10: the Tradeify seven-strategy campaign's whole private evidence base (specs, approval receipt, 125-test replay, canonical ledgers) destroyed with two worktrees; digests only survive. Prior: NAS100 MNQ Pine (2026-07-03), ORB D5 pin (2026-07-31).

title: A green check_brief.py is form-only: adversarially review every decision artifact before ratification
one_line_lesson: Before ratifying any Pre-Q, ADR, spec or closure, run a refute-first multi-lens pass whose synthesizer adjudicates by re-reading source and discards unfounded findings; in the three-seat model this is the Fable escalation lane's milestone job.
cost_if_repeated: SLR-MYM-1 (2026-07-28): both check_brief gates 6/6; a 14-agent review returned 14 BLOCKER / 39 MAJOR — a 16× gate unreachable by construction, an unread §2-A that named the mechanism inadmissible, S1–S6 claimed scored and none scored, an N-basis mismatch, a missing §R attestation, a false bounding claim. The synthesizer also discarded a fabricated venue rule.

title: Three questions per reviewer finding: is the flagged text wrong, is the reviewer's fix right, is my fix right
one_line_lesson: On every reviewer finding, before applying it, verify independently against source that the flagged text is wrong, that the proposed replacement is right, and that your own replacement is right; passing the first does not license skipping the other two.
cost_if_repeated: PRs #282/#285 (2026-09-03): 6 of 15 review findings became fresh defects landed inside the fix.

status_note: 2026-09-20 migration from the Claude-memory store into methodology_lessons.md (light format); memory twin named in memory_twin
title: External handoffs narrate repo state that is not true; Rule-0-verify every path and every claimed edit before acting
one_line_lesson: Before acting on or committing any external handoff, verify every referenced path exists and re-read every claimed edit's target region; treat advisor revisions and self-attributed completions as claims; a handoff asserting repo state the worker cannot verify returns NEEDS_CONTEXT.
cost_if_repeated: Seven instances 2026-06-06 → 2026-07-11 (the most-fired lesson in this repo's memory): phantom files, self-attributed fixes that never landed, a mirror asserted DONE that did not exist, a rule built on a confabulated premise.

title: Capture the test exit code on the next line and confirm the test paths exist before a test → commit → push chain
one_line_lesson: ls the test paths before chaining (a wrong path is rc 4, not a visible failure); capture the code immediately (pytest …; rc=$? or set -o pipefail); better, run the tests in one call and commit in the next so the evidence is read before the message is written.
cost_if_repeated: PR #401 commit e5f44e8 (2026-09-16): a chain committed and pushed 'skill suites pass' after pytest exited 4 on a non-existent directory; tail masked it and PIPESTATUS referred to the echo.

status_note: 2026-09-20 migration from the Claude-memory store into methodology_lessons.md (light format); memory twin named in memory_twin
title: Governance is stress-tested by agent count, not by any one mistake: prefer structural fixes that scale over vigilance fixes that re-pay per instance
one_line_lesson: For any new control, convention or artifact shape ask whether it scales with agent count or its cost grows per instance; generate from source, gate a label to its referent, retain a tested primitive — 'review harder, remember to check' re-pays every time and compounds with every added author.
cost_if_repeated: 2026-08-29 (~40 commits / ~30 PRs from three harnesses in one day): a parser patched four times, one per wrap shape, versus REPO_MAP §2.1 generated from source once and never drifting again.

status_note: 2026-09-20 migration from the Claude-memory store into methodology_lessons.md (light format); memory twin named in memory_twin
title: Codex's PR-level review is the adversarial-review step; do not duplicate it in chat before opening the PR
one_line_lesson: For work headed into a PR, go from drafting to commit → push → open/update PR and let the PR review surface issues; in-chat multi-lens review stays for work outside a PR cycle and for the ratification gate (M-42), which the diff reviewer does not cover.
cost_if_repeated: Operator ruling 2026-08-30, interrupting an in-chat Workflow launch; running both is redundant spend on a review that already fires at PR time.

title: The push is the deliverable: push a landed fix before PR-body prose or long replies
one_line_lesson: When a fix is ready and the PR is open, push first and refine the body afterward; for a gate that fails locally, reproduce it in a clean worktree from origin/main before diagnosing against local state.
cost_if_repeated: PR #282 (2026-09-03) merged nine minutes before a fix that was sitting locally behind a PR-body refresh that did not matter to the merge decision.
